text: Vietnam's automobile market experienced a slowdown in October, with total sales reached 28,957 units, down 17% from September and 24% year-on-year, according to a report the Vietnam Automobile Manufacturers Association (VAMA)

The decline reflects a temporary cautious approach among consumers as manufacturers and dealerships adjust their strategies and prepare major promotional campaigns for the year-end peak shopping season.
By vehicle category, passenger car sales reached 20,715 units, down 16% month-on-month, while commercial vehicles fell 22% to 9,698 units.
Sales among VAMA members alone totalled 22,806 units, down 13% from September and 28% year-on-year.
Passenger and commercial vehicle sales stood at 15,173 and 5,735 units, respectively, both falling 13%.
Domestically assembled vehicles recorded sales of 12,753 units, down 7% month-on-month, while completely built-up imports dropped 24% to 16,204 units.
Despite October's decline, cumulative sales figures remained positive.
Total market sales reached 310,986 units in the first 10 months of 2026, up 7% from 289,331 units in the same period last year.
Imported vehicles recorded particularly strong growth, with sales rising 16% to 176,368 units.
Including VinFast's 200,593 electric vehicle deliveries and sales reported by Hyundai Thanh Cong, Vietnam's automotive market has surpassed half a million units in cumulative sales this year.
Reaching the ambitious target of 700,000 vehicles for 2026 will, however, require the market to maintain strong sales momentum throughout November and December.
